correctness.rationale: A rook-graph edge corresponds bijectively to a P3 of K_{m,n}, and induced matchings correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint P3 packs: any two endpoint squares sharing an original row/column are adjacent in the line graph. Row-centered components consume (1,2), column-centered (2,1); labeled combinatorial choices give N=m!n!/(2^(a+b)a!b!r!c!). The labeled-set exponential formula yields exp(u+v+z(uv²+u²v)/2). A maximal pack leaves residual K_{r,c} admitting no P3, iff r=0, c=0, or (r,c)=(1,1), giving the second EGF (e^u+e^v−1+uv)exp(...). Feasible count k satisfies k<=m,n and 3k<=m+n, so maximum min(m,n,floor((m+n)/3)). Every inclusion-maximal size is ≥ceil(min(m,n)/2), attained by row-saturating stars; equality of endpoints gives exactly nine unordered well-indumatched board sizes. Independent direct conflict-edge enumeration confirmed all induced and maximal spectra on nine boards 2<=m,n<=4, not just final formulas.

value.rationale: A complete pair of ordinary and inclusion-maximal induced-matching enumerators for every rectangular rook graph is a motivated graph-polynomial result, allowing coefficient and optimization extraction. It also determines every rectangle where maximal induced matchings are all maximum—an explicit natural classification relevant to strong matching algorithms.
